# Additions to Daniel Chapter 2 (Susanna) — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition 2: The story of Susanna. A self-contained novella. In Theodotion, it is placed at the beginning of Daniel as a kind of prologue showing Daniel's wisdom before Chapter 1.]*

**2:1** There-was a man dwelling in Babylon whose name was Joiakim.

**2:2** And he-took a wife whose name was Susanna daughter-of Hilkiah, beautiful in-appearance and fearing the-Lord.

**2:3** And her parents were righteous and had-instructed their daughter according-to the-law of Moses.

**2:4** And Joiakim was very rich and had a garden adjoining his house; and to him the-Jews came-together, because he-was more-honored than all-of them.

**2:5** And in that year two elders were-appointed from-the people as judges, concerning whom the-Lord said: "Lawlessness came-forth from Babylon from elders who-were-judges, who-seemed to-be governing the-people."

**2:6** These-men frequented the-house of Joiakim, and all-who-had lawsuits came to them.

**2:7** And it-happened at midday, when the-people withdrew, that Susanna went in and-walked in her husband's garden.

**2:8** And the-two elders saw her every-day going-in and walking-around, and they-were-inflamed with desire for her.

**2:9** And they-perverted their own mind and turned-away their eyes so-as not to-look to-the heaven, and so-as not to-think about just judgments.

**2:10** And both-of-them were-pricked-to-heart for her; yet neither told the-other his grief,

**2:11** for they-were-ashamed to-disclose their lustful desire, their wanting to-lie-with her.

**2:12** And day by day they-watched-carefully to-see her.

**2:13** And they-said to each-other: "Let-us-go home, for it-is the-hour-of-the-meal." And having-gone-out they-separated from each-other.

**2:14** And having-turned-back they-came to the-same-place, and asking one-another the-reason, they-admitted their desire; and then they-appointed together a time when they-would-be-able to-find her alone.

**2:15** And it-happened, while they-were-watching for an-opportune day, she went in as yesterday and the-day-before with two maidservants only, and desired to-wash in the-garden, for it-was hot.

**2:16** And there-was no-one there except the-two elders, who-had-hidden-themselves and were-watching her.

**2:17** And she-said to her maidservants: "Bring me oil and soap and close the-doors of-the garden, so that I-may-wash."

**2:18** And they-did as she-had-said, and closed the-doors of-the garden and went-out by the-side-doors to-bring the-things-they-had-been-commanded; and they-did-not-see the-elders, because they-were-hidden.

**2:19** And it-happened after the-maidservants had-gone-out, the-two elders rose up and ran to her and said:

**2:20** "Behold, the-doors of-the garden are-closed and no-one sees us, and we-are in-desire for you; therefore consent to us and lie with us.

**2:21** But if not, we-will-testify against you that there-was a young man with you, and for this-reason you-sent-away the-maidservants from you."

**2:22** And Susanna groaned and said: "Straits [are on me] from-every-side. For if I-do this, it-is death for me; and if I-do-not, I-will-not escape from your hands.

**2:23** It-is better for me to-fall into your hands without doing [it] than to-sin before the-Lord."

**2:24** And Susanna cried-out with a loud-voice; and the-two elders also cried-out against her.

**2:25** And one of them ran and opened the-doors of-the garden.

**2:26** And when the-servants of-the household heard the-cry in the-garden, they-rushed in through the-side-doors to-see what-had-happened to her.

**2:27** And when the-elders had-spoken their account, the-servants felt-very-great-shame, because nothing of-this-sort had ever been said about Susanna.

**2:28** And it-came-to-pass the-next-day, when the-people gathered to Joiakim her husband, the-two elders came full-of lawless-purpose against Susanna, to-put-her-to-death.

**2:29** And they-said before the-people: "Send for Susanna daughter-of Hilkiah, who-is wife of Joiakim." And they-sent.

**2:30** And she-came with her father and mother and her children and all her relatives.

**2:31** Now Susanna was very-delicate and beautiful in-appearance.

**2:32** And the-lawless-ones commanded her to-be-unveiled — for she-was veiled — so that they-might-be-satisfied with her beauty.

**2:33** And they-who-were with her and all-who-knew her were weeping.

**2:34** And the-two elders stood-up in-the midst of-the people and laid their hands upon her head.

**2:35** And she-weeping looked upward to-the heaven, for her heart trusted in the-Lord.

**2:36** And the-elders said: "While we-were walking in-the garden alone, this woman came-in with two maidservants and shut the-doors of-the garden and sent-away the-maidservants.

**2:37** And a young man who-was hidden came to her and lay with her.

**2:38** And we being in-the corner of-the garden, having-seen the-lawless-deed, ran to them.

**2:39** And having-seen them coupling-together, that-one we-were-not-able to-hold, because he-was stronger than us, and having-opened the-doors he-leaped out.

**2:40** But this woman we-seized and questioned as to who-was the-young-man.

**2:41** And she-was-not-willing to-tell us. About these-things we-testify."

**2:42** And the-assembly believed them, because they-were elders of-the people and judges; and they-condemned her to-die.

**2:43** But Susanna cried-out with a loud-voice and said: "O eternal God, who-knows what-is-hidden and knows all-things before their coming-to-be:

**2:44** you know that they-have-testified false-witness against me. And behold, I-die, not having-done anything of-what these-men have wickedly contrived against me."

**2:45** And the-Lord heard her voice.

**2:46** And as she-was being-led-away to-die, God roused-up the-holy spirit of a young-man whose name was Daniel,

**2:47** and he-cried-out with a loud-voice: "I-am-innocent of the-blood of this woman!"

**2:48** And all-the people turned to him and said: "What is this word that you-have-spoken?"

**2:49** And standing in-their midst he-said: "Are you so-foolish, O sons of Israel? Without examining and without clearly-knowing the-truth, you-have-condemned a daughter of Israel?

**2:50** Return to the-courtroom, for these-men have-testified false-witness against her."

**2:51** And all-the people turned back in-haste. And the-elders said to him: "Come, sit among us and inform us, since to you God has given the-seniority."

**2:52** And Daniel said to them: "Separate them far from each-other, and I-will-examine them."

**2:53** And when they-had-been-separated from each-other, he-called one of them and said to him: "O one-grown-old in evil-days — now your sins which you-committed before have-come-upon [you],

**2:54** rendering unjust judgments, condemning the-innocent and releasing the-guilty, when the-Lord says, 'The-innocent and the-just you-shall-not kill.'

**2:55** Now then, if you-saw this woman, tell me: Under what tree did-you-see them lying-together?" And he-said: "Under a mastick-tree [schinos]." And Daniel said: "Rightly have you lied against your-own head, for already the-angel of God has-received the-sentence from God and will cleave you in-two [schizein]."

**2:56** And setting him aside, he-commanded to-bring the-other. And he-said to him: "O offspring of Canaan and not of Judah — beauty has-deceived you and lust has-perverted your heart.

**2:57** Thus you-were-doing with the-daughters of Israel, and they out-of-fear were-lying-with you; but a daughter of Judah was-not-willing to-endure your lawlessness.

**2:58** Now then, tell me: Under what tree did-you-catch them lying-together?" And he-said: "Under an evergreen-oak [prinos]." And Daniel said to him: "Rightly have you also lied against your-own head, for the-angel of God waits with the-sword to-cut you in-two [priein], so-that he-may-destroy you both."

**2:59** And all-the assembly cried-out with a loud-voice and blessed God who-saves those-who-hope in him.

**2:60** And they-rose up against the-two elders, for Daniel had-convicted them of-false-witness by their-own mouth;

**2:61** and they-did to them as they-had wickedly-planned to-do to their-neighbor; and by-acting according-to the-law of Moses, they-put-them-to-death. And the-innocent blood was-saved on that day.

**2:62** And Hilkiah and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna with Joiakim her husband and all her relatives, because no shameful-thing was-found in her.

**2:63** And Daniel became great before the-people from that day on and after.

**2:64** And King Astyages was-gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the-Persian took-up the-kingdom.
